info.title: Proxmox VE API
info.description:
Proxmox Virtual Environment REST API specification.

Generated from the official Proxmox apidoc.js with validation rules extracted from Perl source across 11 Proxmox repositories.

This spec includes x-since-version extensions on endpoints and parameters to indicate when each was introduced.

host.description: PVE host address

id.description: Replication Job ID. The ID is composed of a Guest ID and a job number, separated by a hyphen, i.e. '<GUEST>-<JOBNUM>'.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

remove_job.description: Mark the replication job for removal. The job will remove all local replication snapshots. When set to 'full', it also tries to remove replicated volumes on the target. The job then removes itself from the configuration file.

schedule.description: Storage replication schedule. The format is a subset of `systemd` calendar events.

source.description: For internal use, to detect if the guest was stolen.

shutdown_policy.description: The policy for HA services on node shutdown. 'freeze' disables auto-recovery, 'failover' ensures recovery, 'conditional' recovers on poweroff and freezes on reboot. Running HA Services will always get stopped first on shutdown.
shutdown_policy.verbose_description: Describes the policy for handling HA services on poweroff or reboot of a node. Freeze will always freeze services which are still located on the node on shutdown, those services won't be recovered by the HA manager. Failover will not mark the services as frozen and thus the services will get recovered to other nodes, if the shutdown node does not come up again quickly (< 1min). 'conditional' chooses automatically depending on the type of shutdown, i.e., on a reboot the service will be frozen but on a poweroff the service will stay as is, and thus get recovered after about 2 minutes.

shutdown_policy.description: The policy for HA services on node shutdown. 'freeze' disables auto-recovery, 'failover' ensures recovery, 'conditional' recovers on poweroff and freezes on reboot. 'migrate' will migrate running services to other nodes, if possible. With 'freeze' or 'failover', HA Services will always get stopped first on shutdown.
shutdown_policy.verbose_description: Describes the policy for handling HA services on poweroff or reboot of a node. Freeze will always freeze services which are still located on the node on shutdown, those services won't be recovered by the HA manager. Failover will not mark the services as frozen and thus the services will get recovered to other nodes, if the shutdown node does not come up again quickly (< 1min). 'conditional' chooses automatically depending on the type of shutdown, i.e., on a reboot the service will be frozen but on a poweroff the service will stay as is, and thus get recovered after about 2 minutes. Migrate will try to move all running services to another node on both, rebootand shutdown. The poweroff process will only continue once no running services are located on the node anymore. If the node comes up again, the service will be moved back to the previously powered-off node, at least if no other migration, reloaction or recovery took place.

Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

host.description:
The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

keephugepages.description: Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts.

keyboard.description: Keybord layout for vnc server. Default is read from the '/etc/pve/datacenter.cfg' configuration file.It should not be necessary to set it.

live-restore.description: Start the VM immediately from the backup and restore in background. PBS only.

localtime.description: Set the real time clock to local time. This is enabled by default if ostype indicates a Microsoft OS.

memory.description: Amount of RAM for the VM in MB. This is the maximum available memory when you use the balloon device.

migrate_downtime.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations.

migrate_speed.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit.

name.description: Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.

nameserver.description:
cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will'
	    .' automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver'
	    .' are set.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

mtu.description: Force MTU, for VirtIO only. Set to '1' to use the bridge MTU

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

reboot.description: Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot.

max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes of entropy injected into the guest every 'period' milliseconds. Prefer a lower value when using /dev/random as source. Use 0 to disable limiting (potentially dangerous!).

period.description: Every 'period' milliseconds the entropy-injection quota is reset, allowing the guest to retrieve another 'max_bytes' of entropy.

source.description: The file on the host to gather entropy from. In most cases /dev/urandom should be preferred over /dev/random to avoid entropy-starvation issues on the host. Using urandom does *not* decrease security in any meaningful way, as it's still seeded from real entropy, and the bytes provided will most likely be mixed with real entropy on the guest as well. /dev/hwrng can be used to pass through a hardware RNG from the host.

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes of entropy injected into the guest every 'period' milliseconds. Prefer a lower value when using /dev/random as source. Use 0 to disable limiting (potentially dangerous!).

period.description: Every 'period' milliseconds the entropy-injection quota is reset, allowing the guest to retrieve another 'max_bytes' of entropy.

source.description: The file on the host to gather entropy from. In most cases /dev/urandom should be preferred over /dev/random to avoid entropy-starvation issues on the host. Using urandom does *not* decrease security in any meaningful way, as it's still seeded from real entropy, and the bytes provided will most likely be mixed with real entropy on the guest as well. /dev/hwrng can be used to pass through a hardware RNG from the host.

cores.description: The number of cores per socket.

ide[n].description: Use volume as IDE hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 3). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume.

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

keyboard.description: Keybord layout for vnc server. Default is read from the '/etc/pve/datacenter.cfg' configuration file.It should not be necessary to set it.

localtime.description: Set the real time clock to local time. This is enabled by default if ostype indicates a Microsoft OS.

memory.description: Amount of RAM for the VM in MB. This is the maximum available memory when you use the balloon device.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

host.description:
The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.
macaddr.verbose_description: A common MAC address with the I/G (Individual/Group) bit not set.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

keephugepages.description: Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts.

cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will'

	    .' are set.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

mtu.description: Force MTU, for VirtIO only. Set to '1' to use the bridge MTU

max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes of entropy injected into the guest every 'period' milliseconds. Prefer a lower value when using /dev/random as source. Use 0 to disable limiting (potentially dangerous!).

period.description: Every 'period' milliseconds the entropy-injection quota is reset, allowing the guest to retrieve another 'max_bytes' of entropy.

source.description: The file on the host to gather entropy from. In most cases /dev/urandom should be preferred over /dev/random to avoid entropy-starvation issues on the host. Using urandom does *not* decrease security in any meaningful way, as it's still seeded from real entropy, and the bytes provided will most likely be mixed with real entropy on the guest as well. /dev/hwrng can be used to pass through a hardware RNG from the host.

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

keephugepages.description: Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts.

keyboard.description: Keybord layout for vnc server. Default is read from the '/etc/pve/datacenter.cfg' configuration file.It should not be necessary to set it.

localtime.description: Set the real time clock to local time. This is enabled by default if ostype indicates a Microsoft OS.

memory.description: Amount of RAM for the VM in MB. This is the maximum available memory when you use the balloon device.

migrate_downtime.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations.

migrate_speed.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit.

nameserver.description:
cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will'
	    .' automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver'
	    .' are set.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

reboot.description: Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot.

max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes of entropy injected into the guest every 'period' milliseconds. Prefer a lower value when using /dev/random as source. Use 0 to disable limiting (potentially dangerous!).

period.description: Every 'period' milliseconds the entropy-injection quota is reset, allowing the guest to retrieve another 'max_bytes' of entropy.

source.description: The file on the host to gather entropy from. In most cases /dev/urandom should be preferred over /dev/random to avoid entropy-starvation issues on the host. Using urandom does *not* decrease security in any meaningful way, as it's still seeded from real entropy, and the bytes provided will most likely be mixed with real entropy on the guest as well. /dev/hwrng can be used to pass through a hardware RNG from the host.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

host.description:
The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

host.description:
The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

usb3.description: Specifies whether if given host option is a USB3 device or port (this does currently not work reliably with spice redirection and is then ignored).

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.
macaddr.verbose_description: A common MAC address with the I/G (Individual/Group) bit not set.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

keephugepages.description: Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts.

cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will'

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes of entropy injected into the guest every 'period' milliseconds. Prefer a lower value when using /dev/random as source. Use 0 to disable limiting (potentially dangerous!).

period.description: Every 'period' milliseconds the entropy-injection quota is reset, allowing the guest to retrieve another 'max_bytes' of entropy.

source.description: The file on the host to gather entropy from. In most cases /dev/urandom should be preferred over /dev/random to avoid entropy-starvation issues on the host. Using urandom does *not* decrease security in any meaningful way, as it's still seeded from real entropy, and the bytes provided will most likely be mixed with real entropy on the guest as well. /dev/hwrng can be used to pass through a hardware RNG from the host.

cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway

source.description: The file on the host to gather entropy from. In most cases /dev/urandom should be preferred over /dev/random to avoid entropy-starvation issues on the host. Using urandom does *not* decrease security in any meaningful way, as it's still seeded from real entropy, and the bytes provided will most likely be mixed with real entropy on the guest as well. /dev/hwrng can be used to pass through a hardware RNG from the host.

keyctl.description: For unprivileged containers only: Allow the use of the keyctl() system call. This is required to use docker inside a container. By default unprivileged containers will see this system call as non-existent. This is mostly a workaround for systemd-networkd, as it will treat it as a fatal error when some keyctl() operations are denied by the kernel due to lacking permissions. Essentially, you can choose between running systemd-networkd or docker.

mount.description: Allow mounting file systems of specific types. This should be a list of file system types as used with the mount command. Note that this can have negative effects on the container's security. With access to a loop device, mounting a file can circumvent the mknod permission of the devices cgroup, mounting an NFS file system can block the host's I/O completely and prevent it from rebooting, etc.

nesting.description: Allow nesting. Best used with unprivileged containers with additional id mapping. Note that this will expose procfs and sysfs contents of the host to the guest.

fuse.description: Allow using 'fuse' file systems in a container. Note that interactions between fuse and the freezer cgroup can potentially cause I/O deadlocks.

cmode.description: Console mode. By default, the console command tries to open a connection to one of the available tty devices. By setting cmode to 'console' it tries to attach to /dev/console instead. If you set cmode to 'shell', it simply invokes a shell inside the container (no login).

console.description: Attach a console device (/dev/console) to the container.

cores.description: The number of cores assigned to the container. A container can use all available cores by default.

cpulimit.description:
Limit of CPU usage.

NOTE: If the computer has 2 CPUs, it has a total of '2' CPU time. Value '0' indicates no CPU limit.

cpuunits.description:
CPU weight for a VM. Argument is used in the kernel fair scheduler. The larger the number is, the more CPU time this VM gets. Number is relative to the weights of all the other running VMs.

NOTE: You can disable fair-scheduler configuration by setting this to 0.

ostype.description: OS type. This is used to setup configuration inside the container, and corresponds to lxc setup scripts in /usr/share/lxc/config/<ostype>.common.conf. Value 'unmanaged' can be used to skip and OS specific setup.

protection.description: Sets the protection flag of the container. This will prevent the CT or CT's disk remove/update operation.

size.description: Volume size (read only value).

searchdomain.description: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if you neither set searchdomain nor nameserver.

ssh-public-keys.description: Setup public SSH keys (one key per line, OpenSSH format).

start.description: Start the CT after its creation finished successfully.

startup.description: Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped.

swap.description: Amount of SWAP for the VM in MB.

tags.description: Tags of the Container. This is only meta information.

tty.description: Specify the number of tty available to the container

unique.description: Assign a unique random ethernet address.

unprivileged.description: Makes the container run as unprivileged user. (Should not be modified manually.)

volume.description: The volume that is not used currently.

unused[n].description: Reference to unused volumes. This is used internally, and should not be modified manually.

cmode.description: Console mode. By default, the console command tries to open a connection to one of the available tty devices. By setting cmode to 'console' it tries to attach to /dev/console instead. If you set cmode to 'shell', it simply invokes a shell inside the container (no login).

console.description: Attach a console device (/dev/console) to the container.

cores.description: The number of cores assigned to the container. A container can use all available cores by default.

cpulimit.description:
Limit of CPU usage.

NOTE: If the computer has 2 CPUs, it has a total of '2' CPU time. Value '0' indicates no CPU limit.

cpuunits.description:
CPU weight for a VM. Argument is used in the kernel fair scheduler. The larger the number is, the more CPU time this VM gets. Number is relative to the weights of all the other running VMs.

NOTE: You can disable fair-scheduler configuration by setting this to 0.

debug.description: Try to be more verbose. For now this only enables debug log-level on start.

description.description: Description for the Container. Shown in the web-interface CT's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.

force_rw_sys.description: Mount /sys in unprivileged containers as `rw` instead of `mixed`. This can break networking under newer (>= v245) systemd-network use.

fuse.description: Allow using 'fuse' file systems in a container. Note that interactions between fuse and the freezer cgroup can potentially cause I/O deadlocks.

keyctl.description: For unprivileged containers only: Allow the use of the keyctl() system call. This is required to use docker inside a container. By default unprivileged containers will see this system call as non-existent. This is mostly a workaround for systemd-networkd, as it will treat it as a fatal error when some keyctl() operations are denied by the kernel due to lacking permissions. Essentially, you can choose between running systemd-networkd or docker.

mknod.description: Allow unprivileged containers to use mknod() to add certain device nodes. This requires a kernel with seccomp trap to user space support (5.3 or newer). This is experimental.

mount.description: Allow mounting file systems of specific types. This should be a list of file system types as used with the mount command. Note that this can have negative effects on the container's security. With access to a loop device, mounting a file can circumvent the mknod permission of the devices cgroup, mounting an NFS file system can block the host's I/O completely and prevent it from rebooting, etc.

nesting.description: Allow nesting. Best used with unprivileged containers with additional id mapping. Note that this will expose procfs and sysfs contents of the host to the guest.

features.description: Allow containers access to advanced features.

force.description: Allow to overwrite existing container.

hookscript.description: Script that will be exectued during various steps in the containers lifetime.

hostname.description: Set a host name for the container.

ignore-unpack-errors.description: Ignore errors when extracting the template.

memory.description: Amount of RAM for the VM in MB.

keyctl.description: For unprivileged containers only: Allow the use of the keyctl() system call. This is required to use docker inside a container. By default unprivileged containers will see this system call as non-existent. This is mostly a workaround for systemd-networkd, as it will treat it as a fatal error when some keyctl() operations are denied by the kernel due to lacking permissions. Essentially, you can choose between running systemd-networkd or docker.

mount.description: Allow mounting file systems of specific types. This should be a list of file system types as used with the mount command. Note that this can have negative effects on the container's security. With access to a loop device, mounting a file can circumvent the mknod permission of the devices cgroup, mounting an NFS file system can block the host's I/O completely and prevent it from rebooting, etc.
